assessments.reasoning: This context directly explains the .jsx suffix portion and path application. It supplies no standalone result for retention of the tested element. The direct archive CLI probe establishes the combined assertion.

The pipeline always adds the TypeScript transform for the assessed non-emitOnly path and adds JSX lowering only if its gate passes. The separately inspected utility limits that gate to React, ReactJSX and ReactJSXDev. The combined output assertion is independently reproduced by the archive probe.

The verified CLI emitted sample.jsx with <box /> retained in preserve mode. Identical text as .ts returned TS2304 and TS1005 with no output. The react-native .tsx control emitted sample.js with <box /> retained, demonstrating that retention alone does not determine suffix.

challenge.method: Replayed preserve .tsx, identical source under .ts, and .tsx with react-native, then cross-checked independent transform-gating source.
challenge.results: Preserve emitted sample.jsx retaining the element, .ts failed with TS2304 and TS1005, and react-native emitted sample.js also retaining the element.

limitations: The source grammar mode, output file extension and retained element are the assessed facts. An output .jsx file requires its own downstream handling. Other JSX modes and .ts input have separate behavior.
